step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture illustrates an indoor positioning system built by Drop Wireless combining Ultra Wideband (UWB) and LoRaWAN. Hardware tags measure distances to anchors and send LoRa packets via a LoRa Gateway to AWS IoT Core for LoRaWAN. From there, AWS Lambda decodes base64 payload data into human-readable format. The decoded distance data goes to Amazon EC2 running a location processing engine to calculate XYZ positioning coordinates. The resulting XYZ coordinates with timestamps are published to IoT MQTT Protocol. Downstream, the data is aggregated and stored in Amazon Aurora for real-time and historical analytics.

graph.name: Drop Wireless Indoor Positioning Architecture
graph.notes: Drop Wireless indoor positioning system combining Ultra Wideband (UWB) and LoRaWAN to track high-value items in manufacturing facilities.

nodes.name: LoRa Gateway
nodes.notes: Receives wireless signals from UWB tags/anchors containing distance timing data and transmits encapsulated LoRa packets over the internet.

nodes.name: AWS IoT Core for LoRaWAN
nodes.notes: Ingests encrypted wireless LoRa packets and outputs decrypted base64 payload data.

nodes.name: AWS Lambda
nodes.notes: Converts base64 machine-readable distance data into human-readable format.

nodes.name: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2)
nodes.notes: Runs location processing engine to compute spatial XYZ positioning coordinates from distance metrics.

nodes.name: IoT MQTT Protocol
nodes.notes: Receives published XYZ location coordinates with timestamps on specific MQTT topics for subscribing consumers.

nodes.name: Amazon Aurora
nodes.notes: Stores real-time aggregated location data (up to 1 time per second) for historical tracking and operational analysis.

edges.notes: LoRa Gateway transmits encapsulated LoRa packets over the internet to AWS IoT Core for LoRaWAN.
AWS IoT Core for LoRaWAN passes decrypted Base64 payload data to AWS Lambda for conversion.
AWS Lambda sends converted human-readable distance data to EC2 location processing engine.
Amazon EC2 publishes calculated XYZ coordinates with timestamps to the IoT MQTT broker.
Aggregated location metrics are streamed from MQTT subscribers and stored in Amazon Aurora.
